newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan stocks seen firmer in first half of 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan stocks seen firmer in first half of 1997/98.

text.p: Japanese stocks are expected to post moderate gains in the first half of the next fiscal year starting on April 1, supported by continued low interest rates, analysts said on Wednesday.
But many said the market may suffer in the next couple of months, citing worries that a rise in the national sales tax from April may dampen consumption and slow economic growth.
Investors may turn their attention to stocks from bonds in the low interest rate environment, brokers said.
"It (the funds shift) could happen at any time," said Masao Ariga, general manager at Daiwa Securities.

"Stocks have become more reasonably priced than bonds. Foreign investors, individuals and some institutional investors who are well aware of that are expected to remain net stock buyers," said Jason James, a strategist at HSBC James Capel Japan.
But some analysts said the key 225-share Nikkei average is likely to consolidate for a while after the government raises the consumption tax to five percent from the current three percent.
"Market prospects are still unclear after the sales tax rise and the ending of special income tax cuts," said Yoshihiro Ito, general manager at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.

"The two major points that we are focusing on now are the impact of the tax increase and currency movements that could affect corporate earnings," said Tadao Sakabayashi, managing director at Nikko Securities Investment Trust and Managing Co Ltd.
Daiwa's Ariga also said further dissolution of mutual shareholdings might dampen the stock market.
But even if the Nikkei average hits turbulence in the months ahead, it will be supported by solid corporate earnings and buying from public pension funds, analysts said.
